newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle market slow $66 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle market slow $66 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle late Monday sold at $66.00 per cwt in slow trading, unchanged from light sales Friday but down $1.00 from the bulk of last week's sales, USDA and feedlot sources said.
About 10,500 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date estimate to 13,400, USDA said. There were no reported sales in Kansas.

Packer bids in Kansas at $65.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle at $67.00 to $68.00, sources said. At $66.00 most owners broke even, but at $65.00 they would lose money, said Dale Benson, analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds.
At the $65.00 bid, cattle owners would lose about $10.00 per head, compared with earning $10.00 to $15.00 per head at last week's top of $67.00, Benson said.
"They're really fighting that $65.00 bid," Benson said.
Fed cattle price weakness was attributed to soft beef prices late last week and the lack of an anticipated rebound at midday, feedlot sources said.

Beef prices for Monday were quoted down $0.21 to up $0.07 per cwt, with 157 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice was quoted down $0.05 at $99.84, down $4.37 since prices started sliding March 25, USDA statistics showed.
